title: Set up Codex and run your first task
tool: OpenAI Codex CLI in Windows Terminal
goal: You will install Codex CLI, sign in, run it inside a project, request a small README change, and review the resulting edit.
prerequisites: A local project folder containing README.md
A ChatGPT account with Codex access

steps.where: Windows Start menu search box and the "Terminal" app result.
steps.why: Codex CLI is installed and operated through a terminal.
steps.checkpoint: A Windows Terminal window shows a PowerShell prompt ending with a greater-than sign.
hint_levels: Open the app used for entering commands.
Search the Start menu for Terminal.
Press the Windows key, type "Terminal", then press Enter.

steps.action: Install Codex CLI by running "npm install -g @openai/codex".
steps.where: PowerShell command line in the active Windows Terminal tab.
steps.why: This adds the codex command to your computer.
steps.checkpoint: The command finishes without a red error message and displays an added or updated packages summary.
hint_levels: Enter the installation command at the blinking cursor.
Use npm with the global flag and the @openai/codex package name.
Type "npm install -g @openai/codex" and press Enter.

steps.where: PowerShell command line in Windows Terminal.
steps.why: A version response proves the codex command is available.
steps.checkpoint: The next line displays "codex-cli" followed by a version number.
hint_levels: Ask the new command to report its version.
Add the --version option after codex.
Type "codex --version" and press Enter.

steps.action: Change into your project folder with the cd command.
steps.where: PowerShell command line in Windows Terminal.
steps.why: Codex uses the current folder as the project it can inspect and edit.
steps.checkpoint: The path before the PowerShell prompt now ends with your project folder name.
hint_levels: Look at the folder path shown before the cursor.
Use cd followed by the full path to your project.
Type "cd \"C:\path\to\your-project\"", replace the example path, and press Enter.

steps.action: Start ChatGPT sign-in by running "codex login".
steps.where: PowerShell command line in Windows Terminal.
steps.why: Signing in authorizes Codex to use your ChatGPT account.
steps.checkpoint: Your browser opens an OpenAI sign-in page or the terminal displays sign-in choices.
hint_levels: Use the codex command’s login action.
Enter codex followed by login.
Type "codex login" and press Enter.

steps.action: Complete the account authorization in your browser.
steps.where: OpenAI sign-in page in the browser window opened by Codex.
steps.why: The browser securely returns your authorization to the CLI.
steps.checkpoint: The browser reports that authentication succeeded and Windows Terminal confirms that you are logged in.
hint_levels: Continue with your usual ChatGPT account.
Enter your ChatGPT credentials and approve Codex access if prompted.
On the OpenAI page, click "Continue with ChatGPT", sign in, choose your workspace if shown, then click "Authorize" or "Continue".

steps.action: Launch Codex by running "codex" from the project folder.
steps.where: PowerShell command line in Windows Terminal.
steps.why: This starts an interactive Codex session scoped to your project.
steps.checkpoint: The terminal shows the OpenAI Codex interface, your project directory, and a prompt beginning with a greater-than symbol.
hint_levels: Start the CLI while the prompt still shows your project path.
The command is the tool’s name by itself.
Return to Windows Terminal, type "codex", and press Enter.

steps.action: Ask Codex to add one short Getting Started sentence to README.md without changing anything else.
steps.where: Input prompt at the bottom of the interactive Codex terminal screen.
steps.why: A tightly scoped request makes your first edit easy to inspect.
steps.checkpoint: Codex reports that it changed README.md and shows a completed task response.
hint_levels: Describe one small file change and set a clear boundary.
Name README.md, request one sentence, and prohibit unrelated edits.
Type "Add one short sentence under the Getting Started section in README.md telling users to install dependencies before running the project. Do not change anything else." and press Enter.

steps.action: Run "/review" to inspect the change Codex made.
steps.where: Input prompt at the bottom of the interactive Codex terminal screen.
steps.why: Reviewing the diff lets you verify the edit before keeping or committing it.
steps.checkpoint: The terminal displays a review of the local change, and the diff shows only the intended added README.md line.
hint_levels: Use the built-in command for examining changes.
Slash commands are entered in the same prompt used for tasks.
Type "/review" and press Enter, then confirm the displayed diff contains only the intended README.md addition.
